Wildcat Sports Weekly Preview

Volleyball looks to improve to a winning record after back to back wins
Cody Rowan, Reporter // September 28, 2026
Graphic by Aiyana Curry.

Women’s Golf

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:45
Instaread

The ’Cats look to bounce back at the West Texas A&M Invitational in Amarillo, Texas, after struggling in their first showing of the year. At the Ruidoso Junior Golf Shootout at Estrella, the team finished 10th out of 16 schools and did not have any individual finishers in the top 20. The ’Cats top finisher was Gabriella Fanucchi, shooting seven strokes over par.

The event begins at 6:30 a.m. Monday, Sept. 28 and Tuesday, Sept. 29 at La Paloma Course.

 

Men’s Golf

The Men are looking to improve on this past weekend’s performance after finishing 11th out of 15 teams at the Bishop Invitational. Chico State’s top finisher was Alex LemMon, shooting one stroke under par. The ’Cats next outing will be in Bellingham, Washington, at the WWU Viking Invite.

The event begins at 8:30 a.m. Monday, Sept. 28 and Tuesday, Sept. 29 at Bellingham Golf & Country Club.

 

Men’s Soccer

The ’Cats have yet to enter in conference win after a lackluster first 10 games. The team dropped both games last week to Cal State Dominguez Hills and Cal State San Bernardino. Both games will be at home this week against league opponents Cal Poly Pomona and Cal State Los Angeles.

Friday, Oct. 2, 4 p.m., University Soccer Stadium against Cal Poly Pomona.

Sunday, Oct. 4, 11 a.m. University Soccer Stadium against Cal State Los Angeles.

 

Volleyball

Chico State Volleyball improved to 4-5 last week after two wins at home. Looking forward to this week, the ’Cats have two away games against league opponents in Cal State East Bay and San Francisco State. The women look to keep their win streak alive and get above 500 for the first time this season.

Friday, Oct. 2, 5 p.m., Pioneer Gym against Cal State East Bay

Saturday, Oct. 4, 5 p.m., San Francisco Federal Credit Union Gymnasium at Don Nasser Family Plaza against San Francisco State

 

Women’s Soccer

The ’Cats got rid of their losing record after an in conference shoutout against Cal State Dominguez Hills. Later in the week, the ’Cats would pick up their first tie of the season after a 0-0 game at Cal State San Bernardino. This week they’ll look to keep the shutout streak alive and get back in the win column against Cal Poly Pomona and Cal State Los Angeles.

Friday, Oct. 2, 7 p.m., University Soccer Stadium against Cal Poly Pomona

Sunday, Oct. 4, 2 p.m. University Soccer Stadium against Cal State Los Angeles

 

All Chico State sporting events grant free entry with a Chico State student ID card or a student’s Canvas homepage.

For information about all Chico State athletics or to keep up with the game live, visit the Wildcat home page or watch through FloSports.
